cs.t: I have an iPad Mini that was supposed to replace books and notebooks, since I travel a lot and travel light. Right from the start, I decided to make it a quiet device. I've had it since 2020, and it basically never bothered me, save for a yearly software update that happens in the background. Not bad! In the end I switched back to paper because physical media is more satisfying to write on and flip through. My iPad Mini was perfectly quiet. The only annoyance is the battery life. The hardest problem in my opinion is separating tools from distractions when they live on the same device. Using the calculator might mean getting sidetracked by a WhatsApp notification. A boring ebook chapter is competing with algorithmic feeds a swipe away. I find that having a separate, offline device (or just a book) allows me to keep my phone a few meters away.

I agree. I've been using an iPad mini with Cellular as my phone-replacement mobile device since the day iPad mini came out. It fits in my pocket (not as comfortably as a phone, but well enough). My only other device is a 15" MBP. To be more accurate, the iPad mini is 7.9", not 7" though. And 4:3 aspect ratio. So in area, it's still much bigger than a 6.5" 16+:9 phone would be.

I would like to update my iPad Mini 1 since it seems like it should be so ancient now (it's had 3 iterations since then), but dammit if the thing still doesn't just work fine. Yeah, it feels a little slow for some things now (especially browsing the internet, can't seem to keep more than one or two tabs in memory), but it's still super solid and gets the job done, and even still works with the vast majority of apps and games. I might have to soon to be able to iOS dev with the newest XCode, but that's the only reason I have. I've owned that thing for almost 4 years now. It's probably the most solid piece of hardware I've ever owned.

I've never hard particularly good experiences with using Windows laptops as tablets, but mostly on account of form factor rather than software. The sweet spot for me is the iPad mini, but I tend to use tablets as glorified e-readers and video players; the only serious work I do on them is reading. With that said, I have zero problem with touchscreens or convertable form factors. In fact, I used a Surface Pro for years as my main laptop, and it was one of the best Windows laptops I've used. But again, I'm not a big fan of mobile devices as primary computing devices unless I'm actually working on the go. Even for commuting back and forth between an office and a home office, I'd rather just put something along the lines of a Mac Studio in a bag — for a few months last year, it was actually a SFF (not micro, weighed about 10 kg) Dell OptiPlex in an aluminium briefcase, which was fine!

It’s a hilarious vibecoded mess but she loves it.  The Adventures of Rollo and Luma, Galactic Rescue Team  All stemmed from her (she’s 4) wanting a game where her stuffed toys go to space. So I started out with creating a canon bible, reference art, style guides, rules for development, the target audience and intent, all that, and then jumped into episodic content following broad seasonal arcs. We’re on season 2, episode 5 right now, and she gets a release every 1-3 weeks. Oh and as a fun constraint it all has to run on a third gen iPad mini. The thing is like 12 years old or something. I plug in the iPad for it to playtest on it with QuickTime and safari dev tools. For me it’s been a fun experiment in genre-hopping - point and click adventures in the vein of sierra, various shooters (all “throw the candy to the alien” or “blow up the lifeless asteroid” adaptations), and after a fair bit of content I decided to hop over to unity. Came up with a pipeline for authoring good 3d assets, from characters to scenery, applied that as a rule, and again, off to the races. Oh and I’ve used elevenlabs for scoring, VA, foley, etc. - all sits comfortably within the $20 a month sub. So. Fun for me. Fun for her. She just mentions this week that the stars at night are really cool, and I have my direction for the next episode.

cs.t: i think about how little i use my ipad mini and yeah, like. its so easy to idealize these pieces of tech in your head and dream up scenarios. reminded of my coworker when he got the surface duo and how much his meeting life was gonna change. he was back on an iphone in like a month, felt like at every corner he was trying to invent reasons to use it but i dont know. it's interesting, im a nerd and enjoy nerdy things... but computing experience in my pocket that's with me at all times straight up doesn't hit the same as i thought it would when i was a kid and thought calculator watches were going to change everything and the idea of a miniature laptop would be so cool. honestly music, gps, mfa apps, texting and phone calls and im not quite certain i need much else. i explicitly left out email there cause email is just better and less stinky for your mentals when you've explicitly chosen to sit down and read it (ie im on my laptop). foldy iphone would be cool but i don't know i guess i'm just not creative enough to envision myself in scenarios where i want a bigger screen during my handset time anymore. if there was some sort of apple pencil as part of it that came with it, that actually changes the calculus just a smidge cause i enjoy doodling. i guess note taking "on the go" might mean something to some, but i supremely doubt apple is even remotely interested in bringing their pencil experience to the iphone.
